title: Classic Lasagne — Ragù & Béchamel
description: A traditional layered lasagne that warms the ribs and calms the spirit.

method.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-based pan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic for 5–6 minutes until softened.
Add beef mince and brown well, breaking up any lumps with a wooden spoon.
Stir in tomato paste, then add crushed tomatoes, sugar, Italian herbs, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cook for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich.
Meanwhile, make the béchamel: melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1–2 minutes until lightly golden.
Slowly whisk in milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Continue stirring for 5–7 minutes until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Season béchamel with salt and nutmeg. Remove from heat.
Spread a thin layer of ragù in the base of a 23 cm × 33 cm baking dish.
Layer in this order: lasagne sheets, ragù, béchamel, mozzarella. Repeat for 2–3 layers.
Finish with a final layer of béchamel and sprinkle Parmesan over the top.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for a further 15–20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

notes.title: Ragù Depth
notes.content: The longer the ragù simmers, the deeper the flavour. If you have time, cook it for the full 60 minutes — it makes a noticeable difference.

notes.title: Béchamel Consistency
notes.content: The béchamel should coat the back of a spoon but still be pourable. If it thickens too much while sitting, whisk in a splash of milk before layering.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: Assemble the lasagne completely, cover, and refrigerate for up to 24 hours before baking. Add 10 minutes to the covered baking time when cooking from cold.
